item.title: GenAI Adoption Strategy for the Enterprise
item.description:
Simple definition#

A GenAI adoption strategy decides where generative AI should create value, which capabilities the organisation buys or builds, which models and deployments it standardises on, how risk is governed, and how people and processes change — so that AI moves from scattered experiments to a measured, repeatable capability.

item.title: Hybrid AI in Financial Services: Practical Decisions
item.description:
Simple definition#

In financial services, hybrid AI means running each AI workload in the place its data, regulation and economics allow: frontier models through in-region cloud for tasks that need the best reasoning, open-weight or licensed models on the bank’s own infrastructure for restricted data and high-volume work, and one governed control plane across both.

item.title: Agentic AI Strategy and Operating Model
item.description:
Simple definition#

An agentic AI strategy decides where agents should do work in the organisation, how much autonomy they get, what platform they run on, how value and risk are measured, and how people and processes change around them. It turns isolated pilots into a governed, scalable capability.
